confirmed_criteria.name: Completeness vs RFP Requirements
confirmed_criteria.description: Every explicit RFP requirement is addressed.
confirmed_criteria.why: The RFP lists seven numbered requirements and puts each one in bold. A buyer who writes a checklist reads the answer as a checklist.

confirmed_criteria.name: Risk/Assumptions Transparency
confirmed_criteria.description: Dependencies and risks are flagged, not hidden.
confirmed_criteria.why: Requirement 7 explains why it is asked for, which is rare. The client is telling you that hidden risk is the thing they fear.

source_refs.quote: inventory decisions will be made based on this system

confirmed_criteria.name: Pricing Clarity
confirmed_criteria.description: Price stated, broken down, easy to follow.
confirmed_criteria.why: The budget is published as a range and states that it includes the first year of support, so a vague price is easy to spot.

source_refs.quote: €80,000–€120,000 total, including first year of support

confirmed_criteria.name: Timeline Clarity
confirmed_criteria.why: Two hard dates are given: a pilot at one site within 3 months and all 6 sites within 6 months.

source_refs.quote: Working pilot at one warehouse within 3 months

confirmed_criteria.name: Data Accuracy & Validation
confirmed_criteria.description: Says how inventory figures are checked against reality before anyone relies on them.
confirmed_criteria.why: The RFP does not list this as a requirement, but it gives the reason behind Requirement 7: stock decisions will be made from this dashboard. A proposal that never says how the numbers are verified leaves that risk with the client.

source_refs.quote: inventory decisions will be made based on this system

confirmed_criteria.name: Problem Understanding
confirmed_criteria.description: Reflects the client’s actual stated problem and goals, not a generic pitch.
confirmed_criteria.why: Worth checking, but Completeness already tests it against each requirement. Scoring both at a high weight counts the same gap twice.

source_refs.quote: 6 regional warehouses across Germany and Austria

confirmed_criteria.name: Scope & Deliverables Clarity
confirmed_criteria.description: Deliverables are specific; clear what is and isn’t included.
confirmed_criteria.why: Same overlap as Problem understanding: the scope constraints sit inside the numbered requirements.

source_refs.quote: no migration to a new database

confirmed_criteria.name: Tone & Persuasiveness
confirmed_criteria.description: Reads as confident, client-focused and professional, not boilerplate.
confirmed_criteria.why: The RFP says nothing about presentation, and this buyer is working through a checklist. Worth fixing, but it rarely decides a deal on its own.

confirmed_criteria.name: Legacy System & Spreadsheets
confirmed_criteria.description: Says what happens to the old legacy system and the spreadsheets after go-live.
confirmed_criteria.why: The legacy system appears only in the Background, never in the numbered requirements, so the checklist will not catch a proposal that ignores it. Someone still has to switch it off.

source_refs.quote: split across spreadsheets and an outdated legacy system

evaluation.summary: Every RFP requirement is addressed with specifics. Two small clarifications, on out-of-hours support and cost after Year 1, would remove the remaining ambiguity.

rationales.completeness_vs_rfp: All 7 requirements, budget and timeline addressed.
rationales.risk_assumptions_transparency: Three concrete assumptions, each with its effect on the schedule.
rationales.pricing_clarity: Itemised €102,000 total inside the budget, with Year 1 support as its own line.
rationales.timeline_clarity: Week-based plan mapped to both targets: pilot in Weeks 1–10, rollout in Weeks 13–24.
rationales.data_accuracy_validation: A 2-week parallel run against the existing spreadsheet process before cutover, stated as the way data accuracy is confirmed.
rationales.problem_understanding: Reflects the 6 sites in Germany and Austria and the client’s goal of not disrupting existing infrastructure.
rationales.scope_deliverables_clarity: Each requirement has its own section with concrete behaviour, such as access enforced at database query level.
rationales.tone_persuasiveness: Confident and specific throughout. The references are credible but unnamed.
rationales.legacy_system_spreadsheets: The spreadsheets keep running during validation, which covers the transition. Switching off the legacy system is still not addressed.

findings.rationale: Critical support only covers business hours. A “system down” issue gets a 24-hour response but only “during CET business hours”, so an outage on Friday evening could wait until Monday.
findings.suggested_fix: State cover for critical incidents outside business hours, for example: “Critical issues (system down) are handled 24/7 with a 4-hour response; minor issues within 3 business days during CET business hours.”

findings.rfp_quote: €80,000–€120,000 total, including first year of support
findings.rationale: Cost after Year 1 isn’t stated. The client will need to budget for support from Year 2.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a line: “Support & maintenance from Year 2: €18,000 per year on the same terms.”

findings.rationale: References are unnamed. “Two regional logistics operators” is credible but can’t be checked.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the sector, size and one measurable result for each, or offer a reference call.
